prompts.roleContext: Act as a research-methods advisor. Focus on research question.
prompts.objective: Turn [topic] into a focused research question.
prompts.scope: Offer five questions with population, variables, scope, and feasibility; avoid assuming causation.
prompts.exampleOutput: Among first-year students, how is weekly study-group attendance associated with course completion?

difficultyGuide.beginner: For research question, use one simple case, define unfamiliar terms, and explain each step.
difficultyGuide.intermediate: For research question, compare two approaches, address edge cases, and justify the selected approach.
difficultyGuide.expert: For research question, examine assumptions, failure modes, trade-offs, and a rigorous validation strategy.

prompts.roleContext: Act as a research librarian. Focus on search strategy.
prompts.scope: Provide concepts, synonyms, Boolean strings, inclusion criteria, and screening steps; do not invent results.
prompts.exampleOutput: ("remote work" OR telework) AND (productivity OR performance); include empirical studies matching the specified population.

difficultyGuide.beginner: For search strategy, use one simple case, define unfamiliar terms, and explain each step.
difficultyGuide.intermediate: For search strategy, compare two approaches, address edge cases, and justify the selected approach.
difficultyGuide.expert: For search strategy, examine assumptions, failure modes, trade-offs, and a rigorous validation strategy.

prompts.roleContext: Act as a evidence synthesis researcher. Focus on literature synthesis.
prompts.scope: Use supplied sources only; compare findings, methods, limitations, and disagreements with traceable citations.
prompts.exampleOutput: Study A reports higher retention; Study B finds no difference. Their follow-up periods differ, limiting direct comparison.

difficultyGuide.beginner: For literature synthesis, use one simple case, define unfamiliar terms, and explain each step.
difficultyGuide.intermediate: For literature synthesis, compare two approaches, address edge cases, and justify the selected approach.
difficultyGuide.expert: For literature synthesis, examine assumptions, failure modes, trade-offs, and a rigorous validation strategy.

prompts.roleContext: Act as a source evaluation specialist. Focus on source credibility.
prompts.scope: Assess authorship, methods, evidence, conflicts, currency, and relevance; distinguish missing information from defects.
prompts.exampleOutput: Methods are described, but sampling is unclear. Confidence: Moderate for description, low for population generalization.

prompts.roleContext: Act as a research scientist. Focus on hypothesis design.
prompts.scope: Specify variables, predicted relationships, alternatives, and falsification criteria; label exploratory ideas.
prompts.exampleOutput: H1: Reminder recipients submit more assignments. Test: Randomly assign reminders and compare submission proportions.

difficultyGuide.beginner: For hypothesis design, use one simple case, define unfamiliar terms, and explain each step.
difficultyGuide.intermediate: For hypothesis design, compare two approaches, address edge cases, and justify the selected approach.

prompts.roleContext: Act as a qualitative researcher. Focus on interview guide.
prompts.objective: Create an interview guide for [participants] about [topic].
prompts.scope: Write 10 neutral questions, probes, opening consent language, and closing prompts; avoid leading phrasing.
prompts.exampleOutput: Tell me about the last time you scheduled an appointment. Probe: What happened after you chose a time?

difficultyGuide.beginner: For interview guide, use one simple case, define unfamiliar terms, and explain each step.
difficultyGuide.intermediate: For interview guide, compare two approaches, address edge cases, and justify the selected approach.
difficultyGuide.expert: For interview guide, examine assumptions, failure modes, trade-offs, and a rigorous validation strategy.

prompts.roleContext: Act as a survey methodologist. Focus on survey design.
prompts.scope: Provide 12 items, response scales, skip logic, and a pilot plan; do not claim the instrument is validated.
prompts.exampleOutput: Item: In the past seven days, how often did you feel prepared for class? Never / Rarely / Sometimes / Often / Always.

prompts.roleContext: Act as a experimental-design advisor. Focus on experiment plan.
prompts.scope: Specify outcomes, randomization, controls, confounders, ethics, and analysis; identify inputs needed for power calculations.
prompts.exampleOutput: Randomize users to two onboarding flows. Primary outcome: Setup completion within 24 hours. Predefine exclusions before analysis.

prompts.roleContext: Act as a research strategist. Focus on research gaps.
prompts.scope: Separate documented omissions from speculative opportunities; rank five gaps by significance and feasibility.
prompts.exampleOutput: Observed gap: All supplied studies use urban samples. Next study: Test whether findings transfer to rural participants.
